title: Kernel amplification & quant misconfigurations — notes and repros
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from the last 48h of debugging a recurring tail-latency regression that only shows up on mixed small/long prompt workloads when we run AWQ and GPTQ variants on the same node. This doc captures repro steps, profiler screenshots (stack traces summarized), hypotheses for the amplification effect, microbench numbers, and mitigations to try. Aim: produce a minimal reproducer + a short playbook so SREs/QA can triage across Dedicated/Private clusters.

Observed symptom (prod-ish):
- 99th percentile token latency spikes by 2.5–4x under a mixed traffic workload (20% long prompts >1024 tokens, 80% short prompts <64 tokens). P50 stays stable.
- Spike occurs only when AWQ-quantized model is colocated with GPTQ-quantized model on same GPU node and when kernel scheduler selects vectorized-32 lanes kernel (k32-vector).
- CPUs show increased system time and CPU-side memcpy overhead during spikes.

Quick microbenchmark matrix (representative):
- Environment: a40x4 node, CUDA 12.2, runtime v1.11.3-experimental, kernel set: k8-compact, k32-vector, k16-memopt.
- Models: 7B-open (baseline fp16), 7B-gptq-8bit, 7B-awq-4bit, 13B-gptq-8bit (light test).

Results (tokens/sec and tail latency):
- fp16 baseline: throughput 14.6k tok/s (batch=8 short), p99 420ms
- gptq-8b (isolated): 15.8k tok/s, p99 450ms
- awq-4b (isolated): 18.5k tok/s, p99 480ms
- awq + gptq (colocated, mixed workload): throughput 11.2k tok/s, p99 1.28s
- awq + gptq (colocated, long-only): throughput 9.4k tok/s, p99 970ms
- awq + gptq, kernel forced to k8-compact: throughput 16.2k tok/s, p99 510ms (regression disappears)

Profiler breakdown (sampling + nvprof summaries):
- During spike, top GPU kernel time shifts from attention kernels -> "kv-compact-evict" and "kv-cache-sync" (combined ~40% of GPU time vs ~6% in normal).
- Host-side: memcpy H2D increases 3x; CPU sys time jumps and blocks on page-fault-like stalls.
- Threads: scheduler worker thread for batch-fusion reports frequent stalling (io-wait style) when vectorized kernels present.

Reproducer (minimal):
1) Start two model instances on same node: 7b-awq-4bit (route A) and 7b-gptq-8bit (route B).
2) Client workload: 80% concurrent connections hitting route A with short prompts (avg 25 tokens), 20% hitting route B with long prompts (avg 1200 tokens). Use steady qps so node is ~72% GPU util.
3) Launch for 10 minutes; observe p99 via tracing.
4) Force kernel selection: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=k8-compact to verify mitigation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (kernel amplification): the vectorized k32 kernel performs well for compute-heavy long sequences, but its memory layout and lane packing cause larger-than-expected KV eviction churn when small prompts interleave with long ones, producing extra KV-sync calls and host-side memcpy. When an AWQ layout (packed scales) is present, the kernel path triggers fallback logic that amplifies cache churn.
- H2 (NUMA straddle + page pinning): colocated models use different allocator patterns; vectorized kernel allocates large pinned pages. Mixed short/long access leads to cross-NUMA page migrations and expensive remapping on CUDA driver, which shows up as host-side stalls.
- H3 (scheduler miscoordination): the batch fusion scheduler mis-estimates per-request cost across quant variants, so it oversubscribes one kernel and blocks waiting for KV availability; blocking leads to bursty H2D transfers.
- H4 (AWQ activation scaling bug): AWQ packing uses a channel-scaling table that in some kernel variants is read with 32-lane gather which hits unaligned memory paths on our GPU architecture; results in slower memory throughput.

Evidence mapping to hypotheses:
- nvprof shows increased H2D memcpy & host stalls -> supports H1/H2/H3.
- Forcing kernel to k8-compact (no vector packing) removes spike -> strongly supports H1/H4.
- Running with HUGEPAGE disabled reduces p99 slightly (~10%) -> some support for H2.
- Running with altered batch-fusion threshold eliminates spike in microbench -> partial support H3.

Quick root-cause theory (working):
- Vectorized lane kernels + AWQ packing expose a pathological combination: small prompt fast paths trigger frequent KV cache updates; vector lane packing expands the write-set and forces synchronous KV flushes on host because of our current lazy-evict heuristic. This interacts badly with batch-fusion that queues many short requests while a long request holds partial KV locks. Net effect: amplified host traffic + kernel stalls => p99 blow-up.

Short-term mitigations (low effort):
- Disable k32-vector kernel for mixed-quant nodes via kernel preference flag (runtime config). Verified to work as above.
- Increase batch-fusion timeout so that short requests are batched less eagerly when long requests present.
- Pin AWQ routes to separate nodes for Dedicated until we fix allocator/evict heuristic.

Longer-term fixes (engineering work):
- Fix lazy-evict heuristic so small-request KV updates are consolidated and do not force syncs mid-token. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2 sprints.
- Review AWQ memory layout to avoid 32-lane unaligned gathers; add kernel-friendly packed layout variant (k32-aligned). Owner: Rina. ETA: 3–4 sprints.
- Add NUMA-aware allocator for pinned pages used by vector kernels. Owner: Oliver/SRE. ETA: 4 sprints + perf testing.
- Add scheduler cost-model that distinguishes quant variants and sequence-length distributions; avoid oversubscription. Owner: runtime-scheduler team.

Open investigation tasks (next 7 days):
- Produce deterministic unit test that reproduces kv-evict path in CI with synthetic small/long interleaving (assigned: Maya).
- Capture driver stack traces during spike with cuda-memcheck and record host page-fault origin (assigned: Oliver).
- Run same mixed workload but with 13B models to see scaling behavior (assigned: Rina).
- Validate whether AWQ packing + k8-compact trades off some output quality; run eval set (500 prompts) to ensure mitigation does not change generation quality beyond 0.5% token-acc regret.

Notes to QA / SRE on triage playbook:
- If p99 spike seen, check kernel selection log (set RUNTIME_TRACE_KERNELS=1). If k32-vector is selected, reproduce with kernel forcings (k8-compact) to confirm.
- Check host H2D mem BW: if >75% baseline, suspect eviction churn.
- If HUGEPAGE toggles alter severity, escalate to infra for NUMA pinning tests.

Appendix: quick commands
- Reproducer workload generator (simple curl-based):
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
    if [ $((RANDOM%10)) -lt 8 ]; then 
      ./client --route A --prompt-file short-prompts.txt &
    else 
      ./client --route B --prompt-file long-prompts.txt &
    fi;
  done

- Force kernel env: export RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=k8-compact
- Perf capture: sudo nvprof --profile-child-processes --output-profile profile.nvprof /path/to/runtime/bin/serve

Closing thoughts:
- This is a good example of a non-obvious cross-layer interaction: quant packing + kernel lane choice + KV cache heuristics + scheduler. Fix will likely require small-to-medium changes across runtime, kernel variants, and SRE allocation. The k8-compact flag is acceptable short-term mitigation for Dedicated customers.

If you want me to run additional isolated kernels or push a quick fixed heuristic to staging, ping in #runtime-debug or add a comment to JIRA-RT-982.

-- Maya
